title: Exploring the Nuances of Infection Control in U.S. Public School Nursing Offices
content:
Infection control within healthcare settings has long been a cornerstone of public health, contributing to enhanced health outcomes, improved quality of life, and cost-effective disease prevention. Similarly, in U.S. public schools, which accommodate approximately 49.6 million students annually, infection control measures facilitated by school nursing offices play a critical role in safeguarding student health and safety. Despite the importance of infection prevention and control (IPC) measures in fostering secure educational environments, significant disparities persist in IPC policies, training, and implementation across schools, placing children at heightened risk of disease transmission during the academic year.
This study explores progressive strategies for advancing IPC education and awareness within public school nursing offices, emphasizing the essential role of school nurses in promoting health literacy and addressing health misinformation and disinformation. School nurses are uniquely positioned to educate students, staff, and parents on evidence-based IPC practices, fostering informed decision-making through accessible, culturally relevant, and age-appropriate initiatives. By countering myths, dispelling misconceptions, and building trust in public health measures, school nurses mitigate barriers such as vaccine hesitancy and resistance to IPC protocols.
Through subject matter expert interviews and a review of theoretical models, this study identifies tailored approaches to address the distinctive needs of school environments. It underscores the transformative potential of school nurses in bridging gaps in IPC policies, promoting resilience, and enhancing public health infrastructure within educational communities. This research highlights the urgent need for innovative, coordinated strategies to ensure safer, healthier learning environments nationwide.
